papers.title: Examining the potential of growing frafra potatoes in polypropylene sacs as a food security strategy in the Bolgatanga Municipality of the Upper East Region, Ghana.
papers.abstract: Populations are denser in the urban areas where there is inadequate arable land for farming. This calls for innovative use of limited spaces in sac farming to produce food to augment household nutrition. The study determined the feasibility of cultivating and comparing the performance of different frafra potato varieties in polypropylene sacs. A Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) with six treatments, each having three replications, was used. Each treatment was a variety of frafra potato, cultivated on a polypropylene sac filled with nutrient-enriched soil. The data collected was analyzed using STATA 15.0. The results show that plants having leaves with the largest leaf area in 2021 (20.54 (8.41) cm2) and in 2022 (19.98 (7.83) cm2) were in the MAL variety. The greatest number of leaves (417.11 (255.26)) were produced by the WAP variety in 2021 but by the MAM variety (349.33 (154.63)) in 2022. Plants having the longest vines in 2021 were in the MAM strain (41.24 (22.01) cm) but in the NAT variety (39.93 (21.54) cm) in 2022. In 2021, the highest yield of tubers was 5.56 (0.23) t/ha in the MAL variety with the lowest yield (1.59 (1.27)) t/ha recorded in the LOV strain. In 2022, the NUP variety produced the highest yield (1.91 (0.40)) (t/ha) with the WAP strain producing the lowest (0.87 (0.50)) (t/ha). The data shows that it is feasible to cultivate frafra potatoes on polypropylene sacs. In the main, all the frafra potato varieties produced considerable quantities of vegetative organ biomass and root tubers with the MAL, NAT and NUP varieties performing better. Therefore, though further investigation is required to draw an appropriate conclusion, these varieties may be recommended for cultivation on polypropylene sacs to produce food for both humans and livestock consumption.

papers.title: Symbiont biosynthetic output tracks host developmental stage in a marine sponge holobiont
papers.abstract: Microbes have likely influenced animal development since its origin, yet how host and microbe partner across ontogeny remains poorly understood. Here we characterise a developmentally dynamic symbiosis in the marine sponge Amphimedon queenslandica by simultaneously profiling host and symbiont gene expression through embryonic, larval and metamorphic development. The transcriptional states of all three core, vertically inherited symbionts were strikingly stage-specific. Metabolic gene expression of the dominant symbiont, AqS1, peaked in brooded embryos, when host glycolytic and oxidative pentose phosphate pathway expression was lowest, and this peak was enriched for enzyme-encoding genes. In non-feeding larvae, AqS1 biosynthetic gene expression contracted across central carbon, vitamin and amino acid metabolism, while its import capacity increased. This contraction was selective. AqS1 genes for the final steps of arginine synthesis, which the host lacks, were minimally expressed in pre-competent larvae and upregulated at settlement together with host nitric oxide synthase, consistent with the known requirement for symbiont-derived arginine in nitric oxide-induced settlement. Histidine biosynthesis genes were instead maintained in the larva, coinciding with upregulation of host histidine-to-glutamate conversion. Host and symbiont nutrient transporters peaked in the same developmental stages more often than expected by chance. In the filter-feeding juvenile, host metabolism and efflux transport reached their maximum while the symbiont transcriptome changed little. These findings show that symbiont biosynthetic output tracks host developmental stage, and suggest that an inherited microbiome may contribute to successive stages of an animal life cycle through changes in its transcriptional activity rather than its composition.

papers.title: Chemogenetic Hydrogen Sulfide Rescues Vascular Senescence in Ageing
papers.abstract: Vascular senescence is a central driver of whole-body ageing, yet rescue strategies remain limited. Here we show that hydrogen sulfide (H2S) bioavailability declines in ageing and atherosclerosis and is associated with endothelial senescence. Developing a novel remote-control, endothelial-specific, mitochondria-targeted chemogenetic system, we spatiotemporally controlled H2S generation and thereby mitigated endothelial senescence-driven programs and reversed vascular remodeling in aged mice.

papers.title: Genetic variation in EIF2AK3 alters astrocyte-dependent stress tolerance in neurons
papers.abstract: Subtle variations in the activity and signaling of PERK, an endoplasmic reticulum kinase, can shift stress response outcomes. PERK has three commonly occurring exonic single-nucleotide variants frequently inherited together as part of the PERK haplotype B (PERK B), which occurs in 28% of the global population and is associated with several chronic neurodegenerative diseases, although its impact on PERK activity remains controversial. We hypothesized that PERK-B was associated with increased activity, altering stress response and stress tolerance, and that minorly but consistently elevated PERK activity, in combination with additional environmental or genetic risk factors, would lead to adverse outcomes. Comparison of stress response between PERK A, the major PERK haplotype, and PERK B in neuronal cultures using novel knock-in PERK-B mice alongside wild-type PERK A mice revealed differential, transient changes. Following ER stress, astrocyte-containing neuronal cultures, but not neuron-only cultures expressing PERK B exhibited similar levels of eIF2 phosphorylation, the canonical PERK substrate at PERK peak activation point (2h), but showed higher levels at 4 to 6 h, consistent with altered kinetics of PERK signaling. PERK-B neuronal cultures pretreated with a low dose PERK-specific activator exhibited increased vulnerability to N-methyl-D-aspartate-induced death compared to PERK-A neuronal cultures, indicating impaired acquired stress tolerance. Additionally, neuron-astrocyte coculture experiments revealed that the observed difference in acquired stress tolerance was dependent on the astrocyte genotype. The association of PERK-B with transient changes in stress response and reduced stress tolerance with higher vulnerability to cellular stress, albeit transient and small/moderate in size, has clinical relevance based on its potential contribution to the overall genetic vulnerability in neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: The global evolutionary dynamics of natural capsule switching in a human-restricted bacterial pathogen
papers.abstract: Exchange of genetic loci encoding extracellular capsular polysaccharides in bacteria can change capsular antigens or serotype, which, in turn, can lead to evasion of vaccines targeting the capsule. However, the evolutionary dynamics and drivers of bacterial capsule switching remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the evolutionary dynamics and correlates of capsule switching in bacteria, using the human-restricted bacterial pathogen Streptococcus pneumoniae as an example, using 10,558 genetically and geographically diverse whole-genome sequences. Our phylogenomic and ancestral state reconstruction analysis revealed that the propensity for capsule switching varies by capsule type and genetic background. We found capsule switches only between ~4% of all possible capsule-type pairs, varying by specific pairs and switching direction. We also found associations between capsule switching patterns and genetic and ecological factors, including nasopharyngeal carriage duration, capsule biosynthesis locus size, and capsule thickness. Furthermore, the genetic similarity of the replacing and replaced capsule loci was primarily associated with the frequency of switching between specific capsule type pairs. Although a few specific non-capsule genomic loci were associated with the propensity for capsule switching across distinct lineages, the collective effect of the genetic background appears to influence capsule switching more strongly. These findings shed light on how bacterial capsule types and lineages undergo capsule switching influenced by genetic and ecological factors, informing our understanding of the emergence of novel capsule-genotype combinations that may impact the design of capsule-targeting glycoconjugate vaccines.

papers.title: The Metabolic Organ Clock: A Computable Framework Linking Cell-Lineage Architecture to Emergent Organ Bioenergetics
papers.abstract: Cell-type atlases now catalogue hundreds of distinct human cell identities across development, each annotated with mitochondrial abundance, dominant fuel pathway, and lineage of origin, yet no computable model connects the topology of the lineage tree to the metabolic rate the resulting organs display in the adult body. Using a curated 396-node human cell-lineage tree spanning the zygote to terminal somatic identities, we test whether organ-level standard metabolic rate (SMR) is better predicted by developmental time (lineage depth) or by terminal fate identity (anatomical compartment). We find that lineage depth explains essentially none of the variance in a cell's metabolic tier (r = 0.11, R2 approximately 1.2%), whereas compartment identity explains roughly three-quarters of it (approximately 75%), and that the mean mitochondrial volume fraction of an organ's constituent terminal cell types tracks the organ's classical literature-derived SMR with r = 0.90 across five canonical reference-man organ groups. These results motivate a five-layer computable framework: lineage as a formal tree grammar, information-theoretic structure of the tree, metabolic switches as runtime operators, compilation to organ-level energetic networks, and execution as organism-level bioenergetics. We also introduce the metabolic commitment-horizon model: the hypothesis that a cell's metabolic tier is fixed at a discrete lineage-commitment event and thereafter held constant, rather than accumulated continuously with differentiation time. In a worked held-out test (5-fold cross-validation, n = 396), a nearest-commitment-ancestor predictor beat a global-mean null (MAE 0.752 vs 0.809, p = 0.015) but was not significantly better than a lineage-depth regression (delta MAE = -0.042, 95% CI -0.098 to +0.012, p = 0.175), so we report the commitment-horizon model as supported descriptively but not yet discriminated predictively on these data. We connect this within-species result to the classical, cross-species rate-of-living hypothesis, treat insulin resistance as an acquired perturbation of the clock, survey machine-learning and deep-learning tools that could extend the framework on primary single-cell data, and close with eight testable predictions and falsification conditions.

papers.title: Night-break photoperiod timing shapes growth trajectories, functional phenotype, and biomass partitioning in Cannabis sativa L. in a genotype-dependent manner
papers.abstract: Cannabis sativa L. cultivation in tropical regions or under indoor conditions requires supplemental lighting to maintain plant yields. Night-break (NB) photoperiods offer a cost-effective alternative to conventional day extension, although genotypic responses have not been clearly described. This study evaluated the effects of continuous and pulsed NB treatments on the growth, phenology, physiology, productivity, and cannabinoid accumulation of three Cannabis sativa genotypes representing two chemotypes. Plants were exposed to a commercial 18-h photoperiod (T1), a continuous 1-h NB (T2), or four 15-min NB pulses (T3) with equal total duration. Continuous NB produced responses comparable to the commercial photoperiod. In contrast, pulsed NB accelerated phenological progression by two to three weeks and reduced final plant height by 15-28%, depending on genotype, without impairing photosynthetic performance or decreasing floral dry biomass. Harvest index increased under both NB treatments, indicating enhanced biomass allocation to reproductive structures, while cannabinoid accumulation remained primarily genotype-dependent with only minor treatment-specific modulation. These findings demonstrate that NB efficacy depends not only on the duration of nocturnal light but also on its temporal distribution, highlighting temporal organization of nocturnal light as a key regulator of photoperiodic responses and a promising strategy for optimizing cannabis cultivation.

papers.title: Single-Cell Omics to Uncover Cell-Type-Specific Gene Regulatory Networks Driving Mucilage Production in Specialized Roots
papers.abstract: Aerial roots of certain maize (Zea mays) and sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) genotypes secrete a carbohydrate-rich mucilage that sustains nitrogen-fixing bacteria, and the underground roots of most plants secrete mucilage at their tips. In both settings, border cells released from the root cap produce this mucilage, yet the genes controlling their formation remain largely unknown. We sequenced the RNA of about 23,000 nuclei from mucilage-secreting roots of maize, sorghum, and Medicago truncatula, sampled before and after secretion. Each species yielded 10 to 15 clusters, which we annotated with published markers and with new markers that we validated by in situ hybridization in the two cereals and by promoter-reporter fusions in M. truncatula. We then inferred modular and cell type-specific gene regulatory networks. Transcriptional programs diverged across the three species except in the quiescent center and the meristem, and in the clusters containing border cells, where a shared set of regulators emerged. Silencing three of five candidate regulators reduced border cell number, while silencing a partially overlapping set of three regulators reduced root diameter in M. truncatula. Silencing the C2H2 zinc finger protein MtrunA17_Chr1g0148421 also reduced border cell viability. A maize insertion mutant of bzip89 released fewer border cells than the wild type. These networks offer entry points for tuning mucilage production in cereal and legume crops.

papers.title: Targeting REV7 exposes a mitotic vulnerability in colorectal cancer cells
papers.abstract: Therapeutic resistance remains a barrier to durable treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC), highlighting the need to identify vulnerabilities in resistant tumor cells. REV7 (MAD2L2) is a multifunctional genome-maintenance protein with established roles in REV3-dependent translesion synthesis (TLS) as well as mitotic progression, spindle organization, and chromosome segregation. Although perturbing REV7 dependent DNA damage tolerance has emerged as a strategy to overcome chemoresistance, whether pharmacologic targeting of REV7 exposes vulnerabilities to mitotic disruption remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the REV7 targeting small molecule inhibitor C10, which disrupts the REV7 and REV3 interaction, and found that C10 sensitized HCT116 and HT29 CRC cells to the microtubule-disrupting agent colchicine, resulting in markedly reduced clonogenic survival. In contrast, C10 did not substantially enhance sensitivity to cisplatin. Genetic loss of REV7 similarly increased sensitivity to colchicine, independently supporting a REV7 dependent vulnerability to microtubule disruption. Combined C10 and colchicine treatment was associated with pronounced alterations in mitotic and post-mitotic nuclear morphology, including condensed/mitotic-like and multinucleated configurations, and increased micronucleus formation. In HT29 cells, combined treatment also increased the frequency of cells containing multiple gamma tubulin positive foci, consistent with disrupted centrosome-associated organization. Together, these findings support a model in which REV7 dependent functions contribute to cellular tolerance and recovery from microtubule mediated mitotic stress, whereas REV7 and REV3 disruption renders CRC cells vulnerable to mitotic perturbation. This study broadens the potential consequences of targeting REV7 beyond its canonical role in TLS and suggests that combining REV7 directed inhibition with mitotic perturbation warrants further investigation as a therapeutic strategy in CRC and potentially other cancers.

papers.title: Cell-of-origin shapes tumor subtype in BRCA1-associated triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: Pathogenic germline BRCA1 variants greatly increase lifetime breast cancer risk, with no targeted prevention. Accrual of mutations following DNA repair errors in luminal progenitors is considered the chief mechanism of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) initiation, which cannot explain the organ specificity nor the phenotypic spectrum of the disease. Here we show that TNBC also originates in basal-myoepithelial cells, and that the cell of origin shapes TNBC subtype through aberrant epithelial differentiation, likely due to pleiotropic role of BRCA1 in regulating hormone signaling. Single-cell RNA sequencing of 67,001 cells from Wap-Cre Brca1/p53 mice and reanalysis of published Blg-Cre data show that aberrant basal-myoepithelial differentiation (Wap-Cre) generates the mesenchymal subtype (TNBC-M) and aberrant luminal differentiation (Blg-Cre) the basal-like subtype (TNBC-BL1). We also show that both subtypes occur at comparable frequency in BRCA1 carriers. Aberrant basal-myoepithelial differentiation precedes tumor formation, and only tumors derived from transplanted basal cells reproduce the basal-containing phenotype of spontaneous tumors. Comparison with a developmental atlas identifies de-differentiation of myoepithelial cells into basal cells lacking myoepithelial markers, a fetal state, whereas experimental metastases shift toward luminal states while retaining a TNBC-M-like transcriptional program. These findings support the inclusion of basal-myoepithelial and luminal cells in targeted prevention strategies for BRCA1 carriers, and adoption of TNBC subtyping for patient stratification and improving outcomes.

papers.title: Tumor suppressor-like mutations mark a dosage-constrained dependency in leukemia
papers.abstract: Cancer genes are classically categorized as oncogenes or tumor suppressors based on whether gain or loss of function promotes malignancy. Here we show that oncogene-imposed dosage constraints can produce mutations that mimic tumor suppressor loss yet mark essential genes. In acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), the transcription factor EBF3 gene harbors recurrent heterozygous loss-of-function mutations, a tumor suppressor signature, and is essential for APL survival. We resolve this paradox by showing that while PML::RARA, the fusion oncoprotein defining APL, drives EBF3 expression, excess EBF3 suppresses proliferation. Patient mutations reduce EBF3 activity through heterozygous inactivation, optimizing its expression within a corridor bounded by fitness constraints at both extremes. PML::RARA activates EBF3 via a p300-dependent intronic enhancer, and p300 inhibition exploits this constraint by suppressing EBF3 below the viability threshold. Our findings reveal that oncogenes can impose dosage constraints that drive adaptive mutations conventionally misclassified as tumor suppressor loss, with implications for interpreting cancer genomes.

papers.title: CDX2 Drives Divergent Regional Programs During Intestinal Development and Redeploys Them During Regeneration
papers.abstract: Region-specific transcription factors (TFs) establish small intestinal and colonic identity, yet what activates their region-specific expression during development is unresolved. Moreover, discrete fetal gene sets reactivate during post-injury regeneration, but their full scope, and what reactivates the programs required to restore regional identity and tissue structure, remain unclear. By determining CDX2 and partner TF binding, enhancer activity, and gene expression dynamics across intestinal regions, in stem and differentiating cells, and through development and adult regeneration, here we show that CDX2, despite uniform expression across the fetal and adult intestinal epithelium, organizes a hierarchical enhancer network. This network cooperates with partner factors such as CTCF to establish a shared, plastic fetal enhancer landscape, which resolves into region-specific programs upstream of regional TFs. During regeneration, rather than reactivating a general fetal state, CDX2 selectively rebinds many region-specific and common enhancers for genes associated with fetal cell-motility and tissue-morphogenesis signatures along with a more recently active adult stem-cell program, each deployed across distinct crypt tiers. CDX2 thus functions as a central, context-responsive regulator, deploying fetal, adult stem-cell differentiation, and regenerative programs as tissue context requires.

papers.title: MAFA drives pancreatic islet maturation through coordination of cell growth, metabolic maturation, and resilience to stress.
papers.abstract: Stem cell-derived islets (SC-islets) are a promising source for replacing the loss of insulin-secreting {beta} cells in insulin-dependent diabetes patients, but compared to their primary human counter parts, SC-islets are considered functionally immature and do not immediately regulate blood glucose after transplantation. To better understand the molecular underpinnings of {beta} cell maturation, we genetically engineered human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) to control the induction of the {beta} cell-maturing transcription factor MAFA or a MAFA S64F mutant variant associated with premature {beta} cell aging and senescence in SC-islets. We employ a combination of in vitro assays, multi-omics analyses, and murine in vivo transplantation studies to demonstrate that MAFA remodeling of the SC-islet transcriptional landscape promotes SC-islet biogenesis and metabolic maturation giving rise to greater SC-islet resilience and insulin secretory capacity. Parallel MAFA S64F studies highlight the importance for compensatory mechanisms for sustaining accelerated oxidative metabolism and enhanced insulin secretion without inducing intracellular stress responses and islet dysfunction. Overall, these results reveal MAFA-governed transcriptional changes that drive SC-islet functional maturation, which provides the foundation for maturing SC-islets in vitro, preserving {beta} cell integrity, and improving SC-islet cell replacement therapies.

papers.title: Declining ribosome function limits oocyte longevity
papers.abstract: Protein synthesis declines with age across many tissues, but whether this decline actively contributes to physiological aging remains unclear. Oocytes may be particularly vulnerable because they rely on ribosomes synthesized during growth and maintained for prolonged periods without continual replacement. Here we show that declining translational capacity is a causal component of oocyte aging. An unbiased genetic screen identified ribosome dosage as a major determinant of oocyte longevity, and experimentally reducing ribosome abundance was sufficient to accelerate the loss of developmental competence and prematurely recapitulate meiotic defects that arise during natural aging, while also producing defects in early embryonic development. Ribosomes isolated from aged Drosophila oocytes exhibit ~50% lower translational activity despite only a modest reduction in ribosome abundance and preserved gross structure and composition, with both ribosomal subunits contributing to this functional decline. Protein synthesis also declines markedly in aged metaphase-I mouse oocytes. Together, these findings identify long-lived translational machinery as an intrinsic vulnerability of the oocyte and establish declining ribosome function as a mechanistic contributor to reproductive aging.

papers.title: Proteasomal surveillance of exposed cysteines
papers.abstract: Cysteine residues are critical for both the catalytic activity and structural stability of many proteins, yet their high chemical reactivity threatens proteome integrity. Whether cells have specialized mechanisms to recognize and eliminate proteins with aberrant or exposed cysteines is unknown. By systematically analyzing the stability of thousands of cysteine-containing peptides, here we identify two complementary surveillance mechanisms targeting proteins with exposed cysteine residues. First, a set of E3 ubiquitin ligases, including AMBRA1, TRPC4AP, FBXO3, and FBXO21, detects double cysteines and targets proteins for ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation. Second, the PSMD14/Rpn11 subunit of the 26S proteasome recognizes exposed cysteines in a ubiquitin-independent manner. Both pathways function in quality control to clear misfolded proteins exposing cysteine residues, including zinc finger-containing proteins. Mutational escape from the ubiquitin-independent pathway through dysregulation of ornithine decarboxylase or FOS levels is responsible for two human diseases, Bachmann-Bupp Syndrome and osteoblastoma, respectively. Our findings reveal conserved mechanisms for degrading proteins with exposed cysteines and uncover an alternative mode of substrate recognition by the 26S proteasome.

papers.title: Desmoglein-1 coordinates cell proliferation and actin dynamics to promote epidermal morphogenesis.
papers.abstract: Skin development depends on coordinated biochemical and mechanical signaling to form a multilayered epidermal barrier. Our previous work demonstrated that the stratified tissue-specific desmosomal cadherin Desmoglein-1 (Dsg1) promotes epidermal differentiation in human in vitro models. Dsg1 first appears in the developing mouse epidermis around E14, coinciding with a developmental transition in stratification and the onset of terminal differentiation, raising the question of how Dsg1 contributes to epidermal morphogenesis in vivo. We generated a wild-type (WT) single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas of murine skin and integrated scRNA-seq data from Dsg1 knockout (Dsg1 KO) embryos spanning E14.5, E15.5, E16.5, and E18.5. Six keratinocyte subpopulations were annotated, including a Transitional subpopulation co-expressing basal and suprabasal markers, positioned between basal and differentiated states. Dsg1 KO epidermis exhibited reduced thickness at E14.5-E15.5, but recovered by E16.5-E18.5, suggesting compensatory adaptation. Differential gene expression analysis revealed enrichment of cell-cycle and actin-associated programs in Dsg1 KO during late development. EdU incorporation and PCNA staining confirmed increased proliferation in superficial layers accompanied by altered actin organization and changed cell morphology. Notably, actin and the Arp2/3 actin nucleation-promoting factor N-WASP exhibited marked changes in distribution during early and late development, respectively. Mechanistically, Dsg1 associates with Nck1, an adaptor linking N-WASP to Arp2/3-dependent actin polymerization. Silencing Nck1 or N-WASP reduced Dsg1-mediated stratification significantly, while a Nck1-binding-deficient Dsg1 mutant failed to rescue stratification in Dsg1-deficient keratinocytes in vitro. Together, these findings identify a Dsg1-Nck1-N-WASP axis linking desmosomal adhesion to cytoskeletal remodeling and support a model in which Dsg1 coordinates cell-cycle, cell morphology, and actin dynamics to drive epidermal morphogenesis.

papers.title: Age-Dependent Effects of Macrophage Derived Cathelicidin Antimicrobial Peptide on Bone Fracture Repair
papers.abstract: The pace of fracture repair declines with age, increasing the risk of delayed union and nonunion. Delayed union and nonunion are associated with significant morbidity and even mortality with few effective non-surgical interventions. Here, we identify cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide (CAMP) as an age-dependent regulator of bone repair. Single-cell RNA sequencing and immunohistochemistry demonstrated higher CAMP expression during fracture healing in young compared with aged mice. Global or myeloid lineage-depletion of Camp delayed fracture repair in young mice, whereas Camp depletion in aged mice increased callus bone formation. Heterochronic bone marrow transplantation using the conditional genetic knockout further implicated hematopoietic-lineage derived cells in these effects and demonstrated that myeloid-specific Camp expression is important in the rejuvenation of the pace of fracture healing. CAMP promotes osteogenic differentiation through P2X7 receptor (P2X7R)-dependent signaling, influencing the downstream regulation of NLRP3 expression. NLRP3 expression is also correlated with osteogenesis following Camp modulation in both young and old mice, supporting CAMP-P2X7R-NLRP3 signaling as a regulator of osteogenesis. Together, these findings identify CAMP as a hematopoietic-derived regulator of bone repair whose function is age-dependent, promoting fracture healing in young animals while constraining it in aged animals.

papers.title: The androgen receptor polyglutamine tract sets the transcriptional balance between muscle growth and atrophy
papers.abstract: The androgen receptor (AR) mediates the potent anabolic effects of testosterone and other androgens on skeletal muscle, yet the transcriptional mechanisms coupling this hormonal signal to muscle growth remain unresolved. AR is a ligand-inducible transcription factor whose N-terminal transactivation domain (NTD) harbours a polymorphic polyglutamine (polyQ) tract that, when pathologically expanded, causes spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (SBMA). To define how the NTD and its polyQ tract shape muscle transcription, we combined an engineered AR allelic series in human myogenic cells with super-resolution and single-molecule imaging, genome-wide binding and expression maps, and human population genetics. Under physiological conditions, androgen-activated AR assembles into dynamic transcriptional condensates and drives an anabolic programme in skeletal muscle through activation of the AP-1 pathway. Progressive expansion of the polyQ tract destabilises AR chromatin binding and shifts its occupancy from promoters to low-affinity distal enhancers, tracking with imaging signatures of muscle aging. In SBMA, this culminates in aberrant transactivation of ectodysplasin A2 receptor (EDA2R), a marker of senescence and inflammation, which engages non-canonical NF-{kappa}B signalling to drive muscle atrophy. Silencing Eda2r attenuated muscle wasting in SBMA mice, establishing this axis as therapeutically actionable. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental mechanism of skeletal-muscle homeostasis and open therapeutic avenues for the many conditions in which muscle atrophy is central.

papers.title: Induction of hysteretic chromatin states by CRISPRa reveals locus-specific encoding of transcriptional memory
papers.abstract: Transcriptional memory is a phenomenon that allows cells to 'remember' prior stimulatory history, which can alter subsequent gene expression patterns and shape development, immunity, and disease. Although various epigenetic adaptations have been implicated, it remains unclear whether the mechanics of transcription alone are sufficient to install durable memory independently of complex activation and global phenotypic changes induced by inflammatory and environmental stimuli. Here, we employ CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) to uncouple gene activation from global signaling and test whether memory can be established selectively by a local transcriptional pulse in primary mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs). Key stimulus-responsive genes (IDO1, CXCL11) remain sensitized for weeks after either IFN{gamma} exposure or locus-specific CRISPRa perturbations. Histone PTM profiling links this memory to epigenetic hysteresis involving persistent loss of promoter H3K27me3. Single-molecule chromatin mapping by DAF-seq showed that this adaptation does not coincide with gains in promoter accessibility, but suggests it supports increased transcription factor reacquisition in rechallenged cells. Finally, while H3K27me3 loss appears to be a key hallmark of strongly induced memory genes, multi-omic analyses showed that persistent H3K27me3 hysteresis also occurs at a small subset of non-memory genes. Coordination of H3K27me3 hysteresis with additional cis factors therefore likely shapes transcriptional memory in a locus-specific fashion, underscoring the utility of targeted CRISPRa perturbations for dissecting these responses.

papers.title: Adjacent Z-DNA contributes to the formation of homologous DNA triplex
papers.abstract: Whether the homologous parallel triplex (HP-triplex, formed by dsDNA and a homologous ssDNA) acts as an intermediate prior to DNA recombination remains controversy, owing to the intrinsic instability and lake of experimental data. Here, we report a HP-triplex that is stable at least at 35 oC under protein-free conditions. Two complementary circular ssDNAs were first hybridized at a 1:1 ratio to form an LR-chimera containing both Z-DNA and B-DNA. Then the circular homologous ssDNA (T-rich) was found to easily hybridize with this LR-chimera to form the HP-triplex (strand ratio of 2:1), involving both left- and right-handed triplex parts under the topological constraint. The third strand locates in the major groove and forms hydrogen bonds with both bases in each base pair of dsDNA without obvious strand exchange. Our data indicate that the third-strand ssDNA may first bind to the B-DNA region, followed by association with the Z-DNA region to assemble the full triplex structure. Structural simulations and analyses reveal that topological constraint imposed by the circular architecture raises the energy barrier for strand displacement, thereby stabilizing this triplex. In summary, the dynamic HP triplex can be stabilized via a Z B junction structure that mimics the in vivo one formed by negative supercoiling. These findings demonstrate that HP-triplex may act as an intermediate for DNA recombination, anti-gene strategy, and other interactions between dsDNA and homologous ssDNA or RNA.

papers.title: THE MICROANATOMY OF INTRACRANIAL HUMAN THROMBI BY SINGLE NUCLEI TRANSCRIPTOMICS
papers.abstract: Rationale: Thrombi are fragile, heterogeneous, and difficult to study with available methods, yet understanding their molecular composition and local microenvironment in stroke is critical to elucidating stroke pathophysiology and improving patient outcomes. Objective: We used a novel platform for harvesting and analyzing intracranial thrombi from endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion to define the cellular and transcriptomic landscape of thrombi. Methods and results: We performed single-nuclei RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on three human intracranial thrombi to define their molecular composition and microenvironment. Across 5,143 nuclei, we identified 8 distinct cellular populations, including monocytes and T cells. Monocytes displayed transcriptional changes on gene and regulon levels suggestive of transdifferentiation. We integrated our snRNA-seq data with publicly available single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from asymptomatic and symptomatic atherosclerotic carotid plaques, and scRNA-seq data from healthy brain vasculature. We identified shared transcriptional programs between carotid and thrombi monocytes along dimensions including inflammation and endothelial activation, supporting the notion that thrombi monocytes undergo transdifferentiation in stroke. We also inferred potential ligand-receptor interactions that may occur at the site and time of occlusion. Conclusion: Our novel application of snRNA-seq to thrombectomy specimens has allowed us to uncover the full diversity of cell types present in thrombi, including low-abundance and novel cell populations, and to provide evidence of cellular plasticity and intercellular communication at the site of occlusion. This detailed definition of the cellular populations involved in stroke will facilitate mapping of novel interventional targets with direct functional relevance and facilitate greater personalization of post-reperfusion therapy.

papers.title: Stress-recovery dynamics reveal a separatrix in transcriptomic landscapes across organs and aging
papers.abstract: Aging is often characterized statically as molecular profiles, but how these profiles may affect the capacity of systems to respond to the external environment remains elusive. We perturbed young and aged mice via transient sleep deprivation and profiled transcriptomes from six organs immediately after stress and following recovery. The same perturbation induced complex temporal dynamics for each gene in an organ- and age- dependent manner. A shape parameter distinguished genes that recovered toward control expression from those that continued to drift away during recovery. Transcriptomic vector fields were inferred from these transitions using neural ordinary differential equations, revealing distinct stability regimes across organ systems. Interestingly, that of testis from the young mice contained a separatrix bounding the region within which perturbed state can return toward control. These findings establish transient perturbation and recovery as a framework for probing age-dependent transcriptomic stability and identifying boundaries that determine whether a perturbed system can return.

papers.title: A mechanistic, mortality-referenced biological age from routine blood tests: construction and temporal validation of IQN-BIOAGE-01
papers.abstract: Background. Blood-based biological age clocks predict mortality well, but they are statistical composites. They do not say which physiological systems make a person biologically older, and they cannot say how an intervention would move the clock or whether moving it would change risk. Methods. We built IQN-BIOAGE-01, a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model of mortality-referenced biological age. A systemic senescent load follows saturating-removal stochastic dynamics and drives eight latent organ/hallmark axes, which are observed through 13 routine blood, blood pressure and body size measurements. Death is the first passage of the load over a threshold lowered by poor organ reserve, and biological age (BAmech) is the age at which the reference population has the same 10year risk. The model was calibrated on NHANES III (14,049 adults; 2,736 deaths in 20 years) and tested on a locked NHANES IV 1999 2010 holdout (24,650 adults; 1,867 deaths). Two later versions were accepted or rejected by rules written before their validation results. We confronted the inflammation axis with three anti-inflammatory outcome trials, audited common implementations of the comparator clock, and locked a registration-ready external validation. Results. On the hold-out, Harrell's C was 0.842 for BAmech, 0.842 for PhenoAge and 0.823 for chronological age. The hazard ratio per SD of the biological age gap was 1.55 (1.48 1.62) for BAemech and 1.45 (1.40 1.50) for PhenoAge. Risk ordering transferred across eras (calibration slope 1.01 1.03), but absolute 10year risk was overpredicted (10.4% against 7.4% observed); life-table recalibration moved observed-to-expected from 0.72 to 0.81. The inflammation axis carried most of the gap. A joint re-estimate did not converge and a converged, biological-variation-anchored version narrowly failed its pre-written identifiability criterion, so v1.0 remains the locked primary. The outcome evidence available so far, chiefly topline results from one anti-inflammatory trial, suggested that only a small fraction of a pharmacological CRP fall may carry the risk implied by the model's cross-sectional structure (posterior median pass-through 0.22). Common software implementations of PhenoAge differed from the published formula by 0.7 2.0 years. Conclusions. A mechanistic model can match a leading statistical blood clock in discrimination while adding an organ-level decomposition, explicit statements of what the data can and cannot identify, and a structure in which interventions can be simulated. Because inflammation dominates blood-based biological age while lowering CRP with drugs may carry little of the implied risk, a change in a blood clock should not be read as a change in mortality risk without outcome evidence. Validation is Tier 1 (internal and temporal, within one survey programme); the external test is locked and awaiting data access.

papers.title: Neofunctionalised plastid translocon regulates chloroplast ageing in Arabidopsis
papers.abstract: Protein import across the chloroplast outer membrane is mediated by the TOC complex and regulated by GTP hydrolysis at two receptor GTPases, large and small. The former are the {beta}-barrel-containing Toc159 family of proteins (Sun and Jarvis 2023; H. Li and Chiu 2010; Shi and Theg 2013a; Kessler and Schnell 2009). The smallest member of this family in higher plants is Toc90, which has long been regarded as functionally unimportant due to the absence of obvious phenotypes in early mutant studies (Kubis et al. 2004; Infanger et al. 2011a). It was hypothesised that Toc90 is a relic of an ancestral Toc159 protein from early green lineage organisms (Hofmann and Theg 2003; Reumann et al. 2005). Here, we challenge this view by combining genetic, biochemical, phylogenetic, and in silico structural analyses to show that Toc90 is not an ancient remnant, but rather a neofunctionalised derivative of Toc159, and likely the most recently evolved member of the family. We show that Toc90 physically associates with Toc33 as a part of a photosynthetic TOC complex. Furthermore, we identify Toc90 as a regulator of chloroplast ageing. Our findings redefine Toc90 as an active and specialised component of the chloroplast protein import machinery, playing a pivotal role in senescence, especially in reducing photosynthetic protein abundance. Together, these results highlight Toc90 as a promising target for manipulating chloroplast longevity and plant senescence, with potential to improve crop productivity and yield.

papers.title: AGROtools: A comprehensive modular cloning toolset for Agrobacterium strain engineering
papers.abstract: Agrobacterium-mediated transformation is a cornerstone of plant genetic engineering, yet many crops remain recalcitrant to transformation and its efficiency is highly species- and genotype-dependent. The limited diversity of disarmed agrobacterial strains available for biotechnology, and the technically challenging workflows typically required for strain modification, constrain efforts to develop improved plant transformation platforms. Here, we describe the development of AGROtools-a versatile, expandable, and user-friendly modular cloning plasmid collection comprising more than 75 individual components, that is designed to simplify genetic engineering of agrobacteria. Constructs assembled with this toolkit couple visual reporters with selectable and counterselectable markers to facilitate identification of recombinant clones, thereby reducing reliance on PCR-based screening. We constructed and tested reporter cassettes that are functional across diverse agrobacterial strains and genomic contexts. By linking a visual reporter combinatorially with various antibiotic resistance markers and orthogonal site-specific recombinase recognition sequences, AGROtools can enable marker removal and recycling for up to four successive genomic modifications. We demonstrate the utility of AGROtools by disarming 10 novel wild-type strains, and accomplishing serial modifications within individual strain backgrounds. In addition to conventional recA-mediated homologous recombination, the collection incorporates components for applying contemporary strain engineering approaches, including CRISPR/dCas9 base editing, INTEGRATE-mediated targeted insertion, and phage-derived recombineering systems. Constructs can be assembled and deployed rapidly, enabling isolation of strains carrying an intended modification in less than two weeks. AGROtools provides a broadly applicable resource for accelerating strain development and genetic studies in agrobacteria, with potential to advance plant biotechnology by aiding improvement of disarmed strains.

papers.title: Pasting behaviour of Australian native grain flours: effects of particle size, flour blending, and temperature
papers.abstract: Knowledge of the influence of particle size, blending, and processing temperature on flour functionality is critical for the utilisation of emerging grains. This study investigated the flour pasting behaviour of four Australian native grains - Button Grass, Curly Mitchell Grass, Native Millet, and Weeping Grass - in relation to particle size, wheat flour substitution at various levels (0-30%), and elevated RVA temperatures (95-140 degrees Celcius). The pasting properties of flour fractions (fine, medium, and wholegrain) were analysed using a Rapid Visco Analyser, and water absorption capacity was also determined. Particle size effects were species-specific. Native Millet and wheat had higher viscosity in the finer fractions, whereas Weeping Grass exhibited maximum viscosity in the medium fraction. Button Grass and Curly Mitchell Grass showed limited sensitivity to particle size, indicating a stronger influence of intrinsic structure. Increasing substitution with native flours generally reduced viscosity, except for Weeping Grass, which was less affected and maintained stable viscosity. High-temperature rapid visco analysis revealed distinct thermal responses: most grains showed reduced final viscosity at elevated temperatures, whereas Weeping Grass maintained relatively high final viscosity across most temperatures. These findings demonstrate the diverse functional behaviour of Australian native grains and provide insights into their potential application in gluten-free and composite flour systems.

papers.title: Homeostatic Turnover, Repair, and the Demographic Form of Haldane's Principle
papers.abstract: Haldane's principle relates equilibrium mutation load to deleterious mutational input rather than to selection strength. We study this balance in a homeostatically regulated, damage-structured population where mutation occurs during reproduction, repair restores individuals toward lower-damage states, and nonlinear demographic feedback maintains constant population size. An exact demographic identity shows that load at every time equals excess reproductive effort weighted by mean relative fecundity. Without repair, the equilibrium branch with positive pristine-class frequency is exactly solvable, and along it the load is exactly the mutation probability times the realized per-capita reproductive turnover rate; when the terminal cap is removed, this is precisely the realized deleterious input, for every mutation probability below one. For rare mutation it reduces to the mutation probability times the pristine turnover rate, with the local fitness contrast canceling at leading order. With a finite terminal class the branch instead reaches a closure-dependent boundary collision. Repair modifies the rare-mutation balance by partitioning first-order removal from the first damaged class between selection and restoration, multiplying the leading load by the selective share of that removal. An exact binary solution extends these results to finite mutation pressure: the unrepaired interior equilibrium collides nonhyperbolically with the fully damaged boundary and converges algebraically at the threshold, whereas any positive repair rate restores a unique interior equilibrium for positive mutation; at the no-repair threshold, its displacement from the boundary scales as the square root of the repair rate as repair vanishes. These results separate the familiar competing-transition structure of mutation--selection balance from the specifically homeostatic effects of turnover-dependent mutation input and nonlinear demographic feedback.

papers.title: Fractional Order Temporal Dynamics of Tumor Immune Chemotherapy Interactions: A Reproducible Dimensionless Analysis and a Pharmacokinetic Caveat
papers.abstract: Fractional differential equations are increasingly used to represent temporal memory in tumour immune and pharmacokinetic models, but changing the derivative order without a consistent time scale can make comparisons difficult to interpret. We study a dimensionless, commensurate Caputo system for tumour, immune, normal cell, and drug states. We establish positivity, boundedness, the tumour invasion threshold, and local stability conditions. We then use a fractional Adams Bashforth Moulton predictor corrector method with an explicit mesh convergence study. Two conclusions correct potentially misleading interpretations of the model. First, the equilibrium locations are independent of the fractional order: decreasing the order changes transient time scales but does not by itself alter the model's asymptotic states. Second, after a unit bolus the drug equation has the exact solution C({tau})=E(-K{tau}). Its maximum is therefore the initial concentration, not a delayed peak. For 0<<1, the algebraic tail makes the infinite-horizon area under the concentration curve diverge. In the illustrative coupled simulations, the apparent late tumour reduction at small is consequently driven by persistent modelled drug exposure and must not be read as evidence of superior therapy. All parameters are dimensionless and illustrative; no patient data are fitted. Source code and generated tables are included to make every numerical statement reproducible.

papers.title: Design and Construction of Three Customizable Pilot-Scale Hydroponic Systems
papers.abstract: An increasing number of researchers, educators, and at-home growers are turning to hydroponics as an alternative method of food production, diversifying and strengthening the food supply chain. This has led to a substantial increase in the amount of academic work involving hydroponic production of plants for a variety of purposes, including but not limited to a more controlled and customizable environment than conventional production methods, utilizing hydroponics as a method of wastewater treatment, and investigating the vertical production of plants on a much smaller footprint than traditional commercial-scale production. Because so many unique stakeholders are interested in hydroponics for a variety of reasons, academic studies use a wide variety of hydroponic systems with varying levels of technology and automation, making comparisons across studies and systems challenging. A few institutions have sophisticated plant growth and research facilities, like those used by commercial companies, but these systems are often prohibitively expensive, costing upwards of $10,000 USD for a very limited amount of growing space for experimental trials. To enable more researchers, educators, and citizen scientists to conduct experiments and easily compare their results, this study details three pilot-scale hydroponic production systems (Kratky, NFT, and DWC), utilizing entirely off-the-shelf components, for under $5,000 USD each, that are capable of maintaining the desired consistent temperature and relative humidity levels, and have space for 216, 108 (6 irrigation loops), and 64 (16 irrigation bins) plants, respectively. The material lists and prices are provided along with assembly instructions and general guidelines for each hydroponic system. The testing and optimization process of environmental conditions within each growth system is also detailed, with suggested customizations for potential experimental setups. The authors developed these systems during their Masters and Doctoral degree programs, enabling improved hydroponic research at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. They hope that other aspiring hydroponic researchers can benefit from this work in the development and operation of their hydroponic systems, increasing research efficiency and collaboration opportunities in this field of study.

papers.title: Cyclic uremia without kidney injury drives cardiovascular disease with rapid onset of immunosenescence and heart failure
papers.abstract: End-stage kidney disease (ESKD) is a major driver of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and requires dialysis treatment leading to a unique metabolic phenotype with cyclic transitions between accumulation and clearance of uremic toxins. Although ESKD patients display the highest cardiovascular mortality among CKD patients, the effect of cyclic uremia on cardiovascular disease remains subject to discussion. Existing mouse models rely on induction of kidney injury and do not resolve the interconnected pathophysiological effects of metabolic, hypertensive and endocrine renal failure. They are therefore unable to distinguish uremia-driven effects from well-established drivers of cardiovascular disease such as hypertension. Here, we established a simple, reproducible, and sex-inclusive mouse model of uremia in absence of kidney injury or hypertension leveraging a bistable vesico-peritoneal shunt (VPS). Strikingly, we identify cyclic uremia as an independent driver of ESKD-induced CVD, that induces heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), vascular inflammation and immunosenescence. As such, the VPS represents the first preclinical model that enables investigation of cyclic uremia as a driver of cardiovascular disease.
